newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says expects new mining discoveries.
newsitem.headline: Manila says expects new mining discoveries.

text.p: New mining fields are expected to be unearthed in the Philippines as foreigners invest more money for gold and copper explorations in the country, Environment and Natural Resources Secretary Victor Ramos said on Monday.
"Expect aggressive exploration programmes and new discoveries within the year," Ramos said at a news conference.

Ramos said foreign mining firms are now preparing to invest more in the country after the government approved revisions to the implementing rules and regulations of the Philippine Mining Act last month.

The rules were revised to assuage the fears of environmentalists and indigeneous tribes over plans to allow mining companies from Australia, Canada, United States and Germany to explore new areas in the country.

Foreign firms have proposed to invest an initial $3 billion in new Philippine mining projects, said Deogracias Contreras, executive vice president of the Chamber of Mines of the Philippines, in a recent interview.
More than 100 foreign companies have pending applications for a financial and technical assistance agreements, said Geosciences and Mining Bureau director Horacio Ramos.
Only two firms, Western Mining Corp and Arimco of Australia, have been granted FTAAs, or exploration licences, since the Philippine Mining Act was approved in 1995.
FTAA's are foreign technical assistance agreements.
The law allows foreign mining firms 100 percent ownership in foreign mining projects.
Among the latest applicants are Phelps Dodge, Barrick Gold Corp and Pacific Nickel Holdings Ltd.

"The big players are applying for FTAA while several junior mining companies worlwide have tied up with local firms either to explore new mines or rehabilitate existing mines," Horacio Ramos, director of the Geosciences and Mines Bureau said.
FTAA applicants are required to spend a minimum of $4 million in four years for exploration, he said.
Mining officials said they expect to start negotiations on revenue sharing with other FTAA applicants in the next several weeks with the approval of the revisions of the mining law.
The revision on the mining law was made after tonnes of waste from a mine of Marcopper Mining Corp in central Visayas island leaked into a nearby river in March.
